Bitcoin continued its grueling consolidation below $60,000 on the morning of June 29, cementing a historically bleak month for institutional sentiment. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have now hemorrhaged a staggering $4.06 billion in net outflows throughout June—the worst performance since their inception—with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for 73% of the most recent weekly redemptions. This mass exodus collides with immense regulatory pressure, as the European Union's landmark MiCA framework takes full effect in just 48 hours, forcing major exchanges like Binance to restrict unauthorized services.

The digital asset hemorrhage mirrors a broader de-risking in traditional finance ahead of a holiday-shortened U.S. trading week. Following a volatile rotation out of high-flying semiconductor equities, the S&P 500 stabilized at 7,385. Simultaneously, the 10-year Treasury yield drifted to 4.38% as institutional capital tactically retreated to the safety of the 5-year curve, awaiting Thursday's critical non-farm payrolls report.
